eli (eng-sre): Seeing a surge in p99 TLS handshake for us-east1 API edge routes from multiple customers, started ~15:30 UTC, filing here since support has multiple tickets.
tara (oncall): Confirming, we have alerts for API latency p95+p99 across us-east1-ingress. Error rates for TLS handshake timeouts up ~6x.
kevin (support): Customer reports: API calls hang ~4-6s on initial connect then succeed. Happening from EC2 in us-east-1 as well as some GCP clients.
mike (eng-infra): I ran quick aggregate: per-route handshake+connect median ok, but tail spikes correlate with specific edge POP IPs. I can see increase in SYN retransmits in our edge logs.
sara (netops): Can you paste a traceroute or mtr from a affected client?
kevin (support): Provided from customer: ``traceroute to api.redwood.example (35.201.10.45), 30 hops max, 1 10.1.0.1 0.502 ms 0.431 ms 0.375 ms ... 8 34.120.0.1 45.233 ms 45.190 ms 45.120 ms 9 * * * 10 34.121.5.6 46.001 ms 45.900 ms 45.850 ms``
eli (eng-sre): Noticing some *stars* in hop 9 usually indicates asymmetric drop. Correlating our ingress logs: some client IPs hitting POP A then being handed to POP B across AZs.
deploy-bot: deploy redwood-edge/rollout v2026.03.15 started by mike (eng-infra)
mike (eng-infra): I see a partial BGP flap from one of our transit peers ~15:28 UTC. AS path changed for a subset of prefixes -> route to a different DC, likely causing hairpin / cross-az hops.
sara (netops): Yup, upstream announced a narrower prefix which caused some flows to rehome to a less-optimal edge cluster. That explains the handshake RTT inflation for sessions forced across zones.
tara (oncall): Short-term mitigation options? Can we pin customers to local POP via routing policy?
mike (eng-infra): We can route by origin ASN tie-break and prefer internal anycast steering; pushing a policy to prefer direct local origin for affected prefixes. Rolling a small policy now to change next-hop preference.
eli (eng-sre): Also increase TLS handshake retry window on proxy (proxy-config: handshake_timeout_ms from 2000 -> 6000) so client libraries retry instead of failing. We'll keep low-level SLOs but reduce errors.
kevin (support): I'll notify affected customers that we have mitigations in flight and to expect transient improvements within 5-10m.
sara (netops): Running tcpdump on edge node for one flow: ``13:02:47.123456 IP client > edge: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, options [mss 1460,sackOK,TS val 123456 ecr 0,nop,wscale 7]
13:02:47.223500 IP edge > client: Flags [S.], seq 0, ack 1, win 28960, options [mss 1460,sackOK,TS val 654321 ecr 123456]
13:02:47.223700 IP client > edge: Flags [.], ack 1
13:02:51.000000 IP client > edge: Flags [S], seq 1 (retrans)`` - shows retrans after ~3.7s for certain sessions.
mike (eng-infra): That retrans pattern aligns with the AS-path rehome window; some packets hit middleboxes that introduce buffering, causing TLS handshake to exceed client TCP retrans thresholds.
tara (oncall): Can we add a fallback route to us-east-2 for the affected prefixes to avoid the flaky transit peer?
sara (netops): Adding a higher-preference route to us-east-2 for the prefix range in question now (policy id: NET-2215-fallback). It will propagate within the minute.
eli (eng-sre): After netops change, rolling restart of front proxy on nodes that prefer the bad path to flush stale connections. Command: ``kubectl rollout restart deploy/redwood-proxy -n edge-us-east1 --selector=pop=pop-a``
mike (eng-infra): Restart done for pop-a proxies. Observability: synthetic p99 dropped from 5.2s -> 1.1s within two minutes for affected tests.
kevin (support): Customers reporting improvement, a few still see intermittent spikes. Keeping them updated.
sara (netops): We'll keep the fallback in place until we confirm the upstream peer stabilizes. Also opened ticket with transit provider (ticket# TP-1123) to investigate the narrower prefix announcements.
eli (eng-sre): Postmortem notes to capture: root cause = upstream transit announced a narrower prefix / AS-path change causing suboptimal anycast steering and cross-AZ hops; led to increased retransmits and TLS handshake tail latency.
tara (oncall): Actions: 1) Keep fallback route until provider fixes (owner: sara). 2) Add monitoring rule to alert on sudden AS-path changes for our prefixes (owner: mike). 3) Temporarily increased handshake timeout in proxy, revert after stabilization (owner: eli). 4) Notify customers and include timeline (owner: kevin).
mike (eng-infra): Adding AS-path delta alert to routing-monitoring, threshold: any change for >1% of flows in 2m window -> pager.
sara (netops): Transit provider replied: investigating BGP session logs, suspect misconfiguration on their edge. They've scheduled fix in 90m. We'll coordinate removal of fallback after confirmation.
kevin (support): I'll send consolidated status update to affected accounts and close tickets when stable for 1h.
eli (eng-sre): Leaving this thread open; will update when provider confirms. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
